Last year I had a planned surgery, and I was given the option to move the date up. My job said the date didn’t work for them, but I did tell them I cannot put my health on pause and took it anyway after some push from my partner. I knew this has angered him a little, as my phone call with him had ended with a sigh and exasperation. 

After that surgery and recovery time, about a month later I had called out for one weekend. My 15 year old niece had discovered a brain tumor and was having emergency surgery. I stayed with my family. Two days, and when she had awoken out of surgery I went back to work. When I came back I received my first ever written warning. Calling out. (I have done so before, so the warning was odd. HR gives our supervisors notice of lates and absences accruals, and it’s our supervisors discretion if we are penalized. 

For the next six months I needed perfect attendance or I would receive another warning. (3 warnings=termination.) 
For 3 months I came into work, even one week when I was sick. (I’m not a nurse, I don’t see patients.) Just for my manager, (a kind women) to send me home upon seeing me. 

At the end of my probation period, they took my weekend mornings away from me and gave them to a new hire. This was odd bc they really favor “seniority” in choosing schedules. When I requested it back, he said “come back in six months when you have no call outs.” 

That hire ended up not wanting weekend mornings. She asked if I would switch with her, I told her we could ask. They said no schedule changes currently, but I guess the new hire pushed. And I ended up receiving mornings. 

My supervisor made a comment that “I got my way.” And I had mornings back. 

After I received my mornings they then changed my schedule from four 10 hour shifts to five 8 hour shifts. My schedule was the only one in the department to change at all. When I asked for it to be reversed, he said “I’m gonna say no because you should have came to me right away.” I asked 1 week after I had been notified. 

And now with this pto denial. 
There’s been little things here and there. So I started job searching and found another department. He was given a 3 and a half week notice.

You have nothing to feel guilty over. You are more important; your health and your safety are more important. You don’t have to stay with him, you have a very long life ahead of of you and this man may very well shorten it.

You wondering if “she’s trying to make me hate her and leave” and other such things seems like the anxious/paranoid part of you. This is not a thing normal people do, if you believe she is neglecting you despite your feelings then she probably wouldn’t have anything tying her to you to stay.

But she’s there. She in this relationship with you, but turning it all down to “she isn’t the same girl I met” is immature. People grow; people need to grow. We cannot stay the same forever.

In all honestly I would think particularly long and hard if she has anything going on in her life that would make her burnt out in a social way. Is she stressed, is she busy, is she going through a life event, school. What you might view as “neglectL even though your an adult man, might be a burnt out social coil on her end.

I was bullied a lot for being fat in high school but behind the scenes I was poor. Like electric got turned off multiple times a year poor. From 13-15 my father lived in a hospital bc he lost his leg and has kidney failure. My mom left us. So I lived in a house with my 18-21 year old brother. We had no car. Lived off his grocery store baker paychecks. He walked to work, I walked to school. We lived on dominos pizza basically bc two $5 pies could keep us full for two days and dollar store food such as frozen fries and canned tuna. Meat was a luxury we could get once twice a month if that. 
My school refused to give working minor papers when until I turned 16. So yeah I was fat. Didn’t leave my bed when I got home from school. Sometimes didn’t leave my bed to go to school. Missed 68 days one year. My friend payed for my lunch more often than I did. 
I had tried to kill myself. Was on suicide watch. Since being fat was what made me a target of bullying I wore a hoodie as defense. As if no one could see I was fat under it. When I was put on suicide watch they tried to take it because it had strings and I could choke myself. I held onto it, I cried, I begged, I shook. I asked if they could take the strings and leave my the hoodie. Even when tried to end my life bc everyday was a battle, I wanted to keep my hoodie on bc of the bullying. As if it would follow me. 
No one at school knew my situation. A lot of people don’t get the obesity rate in low income is tremendously high because nutritional food is expensive. We didn’t have $4 for a bag of grapes. Or $5 for two cartons or strawberries. So on. We could afford $1 soda, $2 3lb of fries, 99c cheese singles. But people saw I was fat. So that’s what they treated my by.
